```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Distribution fit for a 90-day window: A sells through the Shopify App Store, where self-serve ads start at $5/day and one developer (Firepush) reported install costs about one-third of other ad networks. B relies on SEO, which rarely pays off within 90 days, or on paid search at a cited $10-14.50 CPC. Both price points are similar ($12-$99/mo), so A's cheaper path to a first paying install matters most.",
    "A has a documented gap in the free incumbent. Shopify Magic does not handle alt text, images, titles or bulk editing, which leaves room for a vision-based, bulk, alt-text-focused product. B's brief admits there is 'no evident wedge' against seven competitors covering every price tier.",
    "A's ongoing burden fits one person better. A is a stateless pattern: a vision model writes text back through the Admin API. B's differentiating feature, daily monitoring of rule and fee changes across hundreds of state agencies, is a continuous data-maintenance job. B's own brief concedes a six-week build would likely ship a static tracker that buyers can already get for $29-49/month.",
    "A's demand quotes come from the exact target payer: solo Shopify store owners procrastinating on product descriptions. B's demand quotes come from adjacent users, discussed below.",
    "Both ideas share serious weaknesses, so these points tilt the call rather than settle it. Both markets are saturated. Neither brief offers revenue or retention data for any small competitor. A carries a likely one-time-per-catalog churn risk."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not match its stated payer. B targets finance and ops leads at small multi-state businesses, but all three Reddit quotes come from individual professionals managing their own licenses: a solo structural engineer, an HR practitioner tracking employee certifications, and a therapist tracking CEUs and foreign registration. None shows a finance or ops lead at a multi-state firm wanting, or paying for, a standalone tracker. The claim that NeverFined and ExpirationOps are small operations reaching paying customers is also only an inference ('appear to be'), with no traction data.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with no proven wedge, and neither shows competitor revenue or retention. A wins mainly on cheaper, faster in-marketplace acquisition and lighter upkeep. A's own weakest evidence is notable: the ADA alt-text urgency ($25k-$75k settlements, '77% of lawsuits target online stores') comes from vendor marketing blogs. A's Firepush ad-cost figure is a single anecdote. Free Shopify Magic and AltText.ai's 141-review lead could leave A's real market very small."
}
```
